initial.tiger:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset: complete original-drawing animation atlas for a toddler wildlife game.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: eight tiger poses, TWO columns FOUR rows. Image 2 is the STYLE reference: the earlier softly faceted low-poly tiger.
Repaint the eight tigers to EXACTLY the simplified sculpted low-poly look in image 2: larger broad flat polygonal colour planes, smooth matte orange material, cream underside, simple black angular stripes, softly friendly natural face. No fur hair, no skin pores, no glossy realism. Keep every original pose and pixel registration, body/head scale, shoulder/hip roots, silhouette and limb angles INVARIANT. Maintain all eight complete silhouettes, same camera, exact chronological rotary gallop, near and far front feet staggered. Every frame must retain all FOUR correctly attached limbs: no missing legs, no fused legs, no synchronous kangaroo hopping. This is only a style change, not a new choreography. Same fixed 2x4 layout and empty margins. No text, arrows, grid, ground, shadow, props, backgrounds. Genuine transparent alpha.
initial.gazelle:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: SIX complete original drawings for a gentle leap animation, for a toddler wildlife game.
Image 1 is STYLE AND CHARACTER reference: keep the earlier warm ochre-and-cream low-poly deer character, friendly small natural eyes, slim muzzle, dark side stripe, small horns, tail. Do NOT substitute a photographic Tibetan antelope; it must look like the same soft faceted illustrated character. Broad warm polygonal planes, matte clay texture, no photorealistic fur, no pores.
Image 2 is only POSE SEQUENCE reference; do not copy its realism.
Exactly THREE columns TWO rows, SIX equal cells, LEFT-facing fixed side camera, same identity, scale and upper body size. Each whole animal entirely inside its own cell with 12% empty margin, no overlap. Ground baseline at84% of each cell, torso x-anchor at50%.
Frame0 standing relaxed, all FOUR long legs extended naturally, feet on ground, not permanently tucked.
Frame1 lowers haunches and bends knees for takeoff; forelegs remain planted.
Frame2 rear hooves push off, forelegs rise forward and knees bend; four distinct connected legs.
Frame3 airborne gentle leap, forelegs reaching separately, hindlegs trailing with slightly different angles; all four limbs remain distinct, no synchronized fused pair.
Frame4 lands forefeet first, knees absorb, hindfeet follow.
Frame5 rises back to standing with four naturally extended legs, matching frame0.
Maintain equal scale and consistent markings; whole silhouettes painted individually, no mesh deformation. True transparent background, no shadows, ground, labels, numbering, grid, border or scenery.
initial.boa:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: FOUR complete original pose drawings for a children's rainforest snake interaction.
Image 1 is exact CHARACTER AND STYLE reference: previous friendly bright green coiled boa, broad faceted low-poly colour planes, ivory zigzag markings, soft cream belly, modest round eye. Preserve this recognisable low-poly character. No photographic scales, no skin texture, no realism, no fangs, no cobra hood.
Exactly TWO columns TWO rows, FOUR equal cells. Fixed LEFT-facing three-quarter view; coils occupy same footprint, same body volume, head identity and size. All complete figures stay inside each cell with 12% margin, no crossing dividers. Base coil at82% each cell.
Frame0 rested: head lies gently over the top coil.
Frame1 neck lifts smoothly into a modest curved S, head above coils, face calmly forward.
Frame2 same lifted pose, a short thin forked red tongue flicks out; tongue not huge or threatening.
Frame3 half-lowered neck bridges rested and raised poses.
Each neck continuous and anatomically attached to coils; no detached head, stretched disembodied neck or separately pasted pieces. Paint the whole snake in every cell. All coils identical centre/footprint so there is no twitching. True transparent alpha, no coloured background, ground, shadows, text, labels, borders or grid.
initial.crocodile:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: FOUR complete original drawings for a toddler savanna crocodile sunbathing interaction.
Image 1 is the earlier low-poly crocodile style reference. Create a slightly more natural adult crocodile in that same warm softly faceted 3D illustrated style, midway between the original baby-cute form and a realistic crocodile. Longer low body and broad long snout, smaller natural eyes (no giant baby eyes), four short sturdy legs, olive-green back with simplified rounded scutes, warm cream underside. Friendly neutral resting face, not grinning like a toy and not frightening. Matte broad polygonal planes, no photographic scales, no pores, no sharp aggressive tooth display. A few small blunt teeth only when open.
Exactly TWO columns TWO rows, FOUR equal wide cells. Same LEFT-facing three-quarter side camera, same identity, size, snout/body/tail registration and 12% margin.
Frame0 relaxed all four feet planted, mouth closed.
Frame1 jaw opens halfway; body/feet/head top remain in same positions.
Frame2 gentle fully open basking mouth, pale warm mouth interior (not bloody), small teeth; four legs intact, not a lunge.
Frame3 mouth returning halfway to closed, slightly gentler gap than frame1.
Draw each whole crocodile as one connected original, complete long tail. Fixed resting body, only jaw action changes. No seam/labels. True transparent alpha, no ground, shadow, water, backdrop, border or text.
